title.narrative: Strengthening Protection, Livelihoods and Climate Adaptation in Madagali LGA, Adamawa State, Nigeria

description.narrative:
The conflict has intensified protection risks, including Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Child Protection (CP) concerns, and Mental health distress. Reports highlight abductions, sexual and physical assault, survival sex, Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA), Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) and forced early marriage as prevalent protection concerns. Vulnerable groups such as women, children, persons with special needs, and the elderly face heightened risks due to inadequate social services and protection mechanisms.
JDPC Maiduguri carried out protection and Peacebuilding needs assessment in July 2024 and found out that 62.26% of respondents showed MHPSS services and food assistance are their top priorities. Urban Displacement and out of Camp populations, in particular, face marginalization, stigmatization, and exclusion from critical protection services, exacerbating mental health issues and negative coping mechanisms. We aim to strengthen Protection, GBV prevention, mitigation, and response by: • Expanding GBV prevention and response programs, including survivor centred case management, legal aid, and safe spaces. • Strengthening protection monitoring and referral pathways for survivors of violence, exploitation, and abuse. • Enhance MHPSS services by building local capacity, integrating community-based support structures, and improving access to mental health care. • Advocate for policy changes and increase investment in social services to improve the resilience of Displaced and host communities.
• What difference in impact will this have on men, women, boys and girls? The project will drive transformative changes across gender and age group and yet interconnected impacts on men, women, boys, and girls in the targeted communities. Given the differentiated vulnerabilities, coping mechanisms, and roles within households and communities, the intervention will ensure a gender sensitive, inclusive, and sustainable approach.
